newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Even though the results of a December quarter survey indicate manufacturers predict production volumes and sales will pick up sharply in this December quarter, Australian Chamber of Manufactures national chief executive Alan Handberg warns there is more otimism than reality in the results. Handberg says performance has repeatedly fallen below survey expectations for the past 18 months. Page 1.

The authors of the new publication, 'The Clever Country? Australia's Digital Future', claim Australian business risks missing out on successfully exploiting the information revolution because its "blue chip" boards are slow to embrace the Internet and other online technology. Daniel Petre, one-time protege of Bill Gates, and David Harrington call on business and policy makers to adjust their thinking to the era of the electronic marketplace. Page 4.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd told the Victorian Supreme Court on Friday that it would consider amending its statement of claim against former Elders IXL executives John Elliott and Peter Scanlon and the Bank of New Zealand in relation to A$66.5 million in allegedly sham foreign exchange deals. Lawyers representing the businessmen said if they received an amended statement of claim, the future of their civil action would be assessed. Page 5.

Addressing a meeting of analysts in London last week, RTZ-CRA deputy chief executive Leon Davis said the company's aim is to treble the productivity of Australian mines to US levels before committing itself to a doubling of its Australian coal output. RTZ-CRA has also signalled changes to annual, long service and sick leave entitlements. Page 21.

BHP has cut copper mining costs to below US60 cents a pound and is looking at new ways to produce low-cost copper metal, possibly by producing metal in mini-smelters at each mine. Transporting a higher-grade copper would save millions of dollars in transport costs and reduce the need for costly large smelters. Page 21.

Although Hamilton Island Ltd has opened the 1996-97 financial year with a A$1.4 million loss for the first quarter ended October 1, managing director of the Barrier Reef resort operator, Wayne Kirkpatrick, says the company is still confident of meeting it prospectus estimate of A$2.1 million profit for the year. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A sober reporting season for the banks begins tomorrow, with Westpac Banking Corp expecting to report a modest profit increase of 11 percent to A$1.09 billion. Accelerating bad debts and a looming revenue crunch will contribute to reports of shrinking pofits which will be accompanied by reports of huge job losses. Page 29.

BHP Copper chief executive Burgess Winter says the blow-out in copper production costs which combined with a terrifying slump in prices to slice A$150 million from BHP's first-quarter earnings has been brought under control by a detailed review. Winter noted that the company's production costs were now nearing the target ranges envisaged when BHP created the copper division. Page 29.

Carlton and United Breweries Ltd head Nuno D'Aquino has let fly at New Zealand rival Lion Nathan Ltd, accusing it of indulging in non-stop price-cutting in CUB's home market of Victoria since 1994 and claiming its discounting of core XXXX brands in Queenland was undermining retail trade in that state which would lead to its unravelling. Page 29.

Australian Law Reform Commission president Alan Rose says the push by business to go international has left it increasingly exposed to international legal problems. Rose says there are significant differences with overseas jurisdictions which mean legal problems are set to increase in volume and significance, tying up valuable management time. Page 31.

Queensland's bancassurance merger group's planning committee chairman John Lamble says the group plans to withdraw support for Metway Bank Ltd's A$30 million core retail banking software joint venture, choosing instead to install the Hogan banking system mplemented this year by Suncorp. Page 31.

The sale of John Singleton Advertising's JSA.AX A$59 million share of the Ten Group television network to Melbourne businessman Isi Leibler will not disrupt the group's long awaited plan for a sharemarket listing. The shares were bought at A$13 each, leaving Singleton with a A$54.5 million profit. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AMP Society will today launch a A$400 million float of six prime office towers. The move by AMP into the sharemarket listed property funds business has been long awaited - until now the giant investment group has kept away from the market, despite aggressive moves by competitors such as Bankers Trust, Colonial and National Mutual. Page 35.

Submissions to the Federal Government's inquiry into the cross-media rules close today. Board meetings were held across the country over the weekend to put the finishing touches on final submissions. The government's decisions will have a strong impact on media ownership, most importantly over the control of John Fairfax Holdings , the Seven Network, the Ten Group, and possibly regional media companies and radio companies. Page 35.

Australian National Industries chairman Ted Harris was surprised at the request by former director Ross Palmer to call an extraordinary general meeting to sack directors Peter Joseph and Howard Stack. ANI's board will consider when to hold the meeting, but is awaiting the findings of an inquiry by Bob Ellicot, QC, into the controversial ABT transactions. Page 35.

The latest Insurance and Superannuation Commission report says the boom in the superannuation fund sector continues to rise, with 2,000 new super funds forming each month and a large jump in the number of women with super accounts. Page 35.

AME Mineral Economics Pty Ltd's 1996 aluminium study said the recently ended Brussels Memorandum of Understanding had delayed the expansion of aluminium production. The study found that world aluminium prices will increase only slowly to 1999 and rising stocks after 1999 could depress prices and create a glut if current production expansion plans go ahead. Page 37.

Melbourne-based mining consulting group Surbiton Associates says Australia is set to achieve record gold production this year. The positive outlook follows gold production figures showing Australia produced 73 tonnes of gold in July-September, the second highest quarterly output ever. Page 37.
THE AGE

Auctioneers Christies is hoping to fetch A$300,000 or more for John Peter Russell's Madame Sisely on the Bank of the Loing at Moret, which has been repatriated from France to Australia, at its big art sale this month. As Christies and rival international saleroom Sotheby's begin to bring Australian paintings back here to sell, Christies hopes to auction other great works including Russell Drysdale's Red Landscape (estimated at up to A$300,000) and Arthur Boyd's Bridgeroom Drinking from a Creek II, which copuld fetch up to A$150,000. Page C1.

A survey of September quarter output by Melbourne-based Surbiton Associates indicates production by the Australian gold industry has continued at record levels despite the lacklustre performance of the gold price. The September quarter weighed in at 73 tonnes, worth A$1.1 billion at present prices and exchange rates. Page C1.

John Singleton Advertising JSA.AX will dispose of its 10 percent voting stake in the Ten Group for A$59.15 million. The deal, finalised after 11th hour talks on Friday night, requires the advertising group to first offer its shares to fellow stake holder as part of a pre-emptive rights agreement. Page C1.

Following 1997 earnings projections which show the WAPET oil group's operations are set to pay a rate of return lower than bank interest rates, as many as 200 employees at the group's West Australian operations will face redundancy. WAPET management will brief staff today on redundancies, but it is believed many job losses will come from the company's Perth headquarters, with some impact on the Barrow Island oil fields and other projects. Page C3.

The AMP Office Trust unveiled yesterday will include 25 percent of the Melbourne office tower Bourke Place, 7-15 Blue St, North Sydney, 10 Eagle St, Brisbane, 111 Alinga St, Canberra and 25 percent of 255 George St, Sydney. The remaining portions of the properties will continue to be owned by the AMP Society and managed by AMP Investments. Page C3.
